verdict.summary: You can create a Dev Dashboard app and connect your own store or development stores in under an hour with no review. Installing on stores you don't control requires Public distribution and a full App Store review, even if the listing is unlisted (limited visibility). That review includes a one-time fee, compliance webhooks, a screencast, specific OAuth behaviour and possibly protected-customer-data approval.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own store; 2-5 days of build and listing work for public review
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own store or development stores. Public distribution: no official timeline; 5-14 business days reported

gates.name: Custom distribution app (your own store or a development store)
gates.unlocks: OAuth installs on your own store or development stores through Composio, using your app's client ID and secret.
limits: Since January 1, 2026, new custom apps can't be created in the Shopify admin. Create them in the Dev Dashboard instead
Custom apps can't use Shopify's app billing
On development stores, protected customer data works without a review submission once you select the data and fields

gates.name: Custom distribution (one store, one Plus organization, or development stores)
gates.unlocks: Installs on one merchant's store, on stores in a single Plus organization, or on development stores. This is the most you get without review.
limits: Only one merchant store, or stores in one Plus organization. You can't share the app with other merchants
There is no unlisted, review-free Public option. Unpublished apps were deprecated in 2019
No published install cap was found beyond these distribution limits

gates.name: Public distribution + Shopify App Store review
gates.unlocks: Any merchant can install the app. You can choose full visibility or limited visibility (unlisted: not indexed, but installable from the listing URL).
limits: Limited visibility still needs a listing page and the full review
Repeated failed reviews trigger a cooldown on submissions, and each repeat cooldown is longer
You can't submit if the app calls API versions that will be deprecated within 90 days
Protected customer data (Level 1 and Level 2) needs its own review for public apps
gates.time_to_reach: No official timeline. Third parties report 5-14 business days per review round, plus a few days of prep

steps.title: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Sign in or create an account at dev.shopify.com/dashboard. New custom apps can no longer be created under Settings > Apps in the Shopify admin. Every new app, custom or public, has to start in the Dev Dashboard.
gotchas: The old admin 'Develop apps' route doesn't work for new apps after January 1, 2026.

steps.title: Get a store to install on
steps.detail: Pick the store you'll test on: your own store or a development store. Development stores are allowed under Custom distribution, and they let you test protected customer data without a review.

steps.title: Create the app with name, App URL and redirection URL
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard, create a new app and fill in the app name, App URL and allowed redirection URLs. The redirect_uri sent during authorization has to match an allowed redirection URL exactly.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: App URLs and the API contact email can't contain 'Shopify' or 'Example', including misspellings or abbreviations. Reviewers check this later, so choose them now.
Composio has referenced two callback paths (/api/v1/auth-apps/add and /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). Copy the exact URL from your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Choose a distribution method
steps.detail: Choose Custom distribution if the app will only run on your store, one client's store, a Plus organization or development stores. Choose Public distribution only if other merchants will install it, because Public means App Store review even with limited visibility.
gotchas: In the Dev Dashboard there is no Public option that skips review.

steps.title: Declare only the scopes you need and deploy
steps.detail: Declare scopes in the app configuration and deploy. Merchants approve them at install. Cut Composio's long default list down to what your agent actually calls. Shopify restricts scopes when there's no legitimate use, and some scopes need Shopify's approval before you can declare them.
gotchas: read_all_orders (orders older than 60 days) needs separate approval.

steps.title: Select protected customer data if you need customer PII
steps.detail: If your agent reads customer name, address, email or phone, select protected customer data plus each of those fields individually. On development stores this works without a review. Custom apps have both levels available.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config and run a test install
steps.detail: Enter the app's client ID and client secret into a Composio Shopify OAuth2 auth config, using the same scopes. Then authorize against your store's myshopify.com domain. Shopify builds the authorize URL on the shop domain with client_id, scope, redirect_uri and state, then exchanges the code at /admin/oauth/access_token.
gotchas: A wrong client_id doesn't produce an OAuth error. Shopify sends you to an admin login page instead, so double-check the credentials if you land on a login page.

steps.title: Register for the App Store and pay the one-time fee
steps.detail: Public distribution requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee. Also add an emergency developer email and phone number to the account.

steps.title: Make the app meet review behaviour rules
steps.detail: Subscribe to the compliance webhooks. Start OAuth immediately on install and on reinstall, beginning from the Shopify admin install. After the merchant accepts permissions, redirect them to your app's UI. Don't ask merchants to type their myshopify domain. Use an API version that isn't due for deprecation within 90 days.
gotchas: Automated checks fail apps that don't start authentication from the expected admin URL at install.
A vendor blog (not confirmed by Shopify) says new public apps must use expiring offline access tokens from April 1, 2026.

steps.title: Request protected customer data before submitting
steps.detail: If you need customer data, file the Level 1 and Level 2 request and the individual field requests in the Partner Dashboard before you submit. You can't apply while the app is under review. Level 2 adds requirements such as encrypted backups, separated environments and an incident response policy.

steps.title: Prepare the listing assets
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy, listing text and setup instructions. Produce a 1200x1200 JPEG or PNG icon and 3-6 desktop screenshots at 1600x900, at least one showing the app's UI. Provide a demo store link and test credentials with full access if a third-party platform is involved. You have to record the full setup screencast yourself.

steps.title: Run automated checks and submit for review
steps.detail: On the App Store review page, complete the mandatory fields and run the automated checks. You can submit to reviewers only once the checks pass.

steps.title: Wait for App Store review
steps.detail: Shopify publishes no fixed turnaround. Third parties report 5-14 business days per round. Fix every issue raised before resubmitting, because repeated failures put the app into cooldowns that get longer each time.

requirements.item: Dev Dashboard app (custom apps can't be created in the Shopify admin)
requirements.detail: Required for every new app since January 1, 2026.

requirements.item: Allowed redirection URL that exactly matches the Composio callback
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri must exactly match an allowed redirection URL.

requirements.item: App Store registration with a one-time fee

requirements.detail: Apps distributed through the App Store must subscribe to them.
1200x1200 JPEG or PNG icon; 3-6 desktop screenshots at 1600x900, at least one showing the app's UI.

requirements.item: Screencast, setup instructions, demo store and test credentials
requirements.detail: Reviewers expect a full screencast and test credentials with full access where a third-party platform is involved.
Email and phone number for critical technical issues.

requirements.item: No 'Shopify' in app URLs or API contact email
requirements.detail: Misspellings and abbreviations are also barred.
Authorize immediately, start from the admin install, redirect to the app UI afterwards, and don't ask merchants to type their shop domain.
You can't submit if the app uses APIs that will be deprecated within 90 days.

scopes.scope: Protected customer data, Level 1 (excludes name, address, phone and email)
scopes.effect: Needs review for public apps; available to custom apps. Requested in the Partner Dashboard, and you can't request it while the app is under review.

scopes.scope: Protected customer data, Level 2 + fields (name, address, email, phone)
scopes.effect: Each field is requested individually and needs review for public apps. Seven extra data-handling requirements apply, and Shopify may run a detailed data-protection review.
Extends order access beyond the default 60-day window and has its own approval rules.
Shopify must approve the app before you can declare them. For some other labelled scopes, the docs say to contact Shopify Support.

scopes.scope: Composio default list (read_/write_ products, orders, customers, themes, script_tags, etc.)
scopes.effect: Requesting scopes you don't need is a review risk, because Shopify restricts scopes without a legitimate use. Trim the list before submitting.

blockers.symptom: No 'Create an app' / 'Develop apps' option for new custom apps in the Shopify admin
blockers.cause: Legacy custom apps can't be created after January 1, 2026.
blockers.fix: Build the app in the Dev Dashboard, then install it on the store.

blockers.symptom: Can't share the app with other merchants without review; no unlisted option in the Dev Dashboard
blockers.cause: Custom distribution is limited to one store or one Plus organization. Public distribution, including limited visibility, requires App Store review.
blockers.fix: Stay on Custom distribution for single-client use, or go through the Public review.

blockers.symptom: The authorize URL lands on an admin login page instead of showing an OAuth error
blockers.cause: Shopify doesn't reject an invalid client_id at the authorize step.
blockers.fix: Check that the client ID in Composio matches the Dev Dashboard app, and that you're logged into the correct store.

blockers.symptom: "During an automated check, your app didn't successfully initiate authentication when installing."
blockers.cause: OAuth didn't start from the expected Shopify admin install URL. Composio-hosted connect flows may not match what reviewers expect.
blockers.fix: Start OAuth immediately on install from the admin and redirect to your app's UI after the merchant grants access.

blockers.symptom: Review rejection for asking merchants to enter their myshopify.com domain
blockers.cause: Reviewers don't allow manual shop-domain entry.
blockers.fix: Get the shop from the install request instead of asking the merchant.

blockers.symptom: Can't submit a protected customer data request
blockers.cause: Requests are blocked while the app is under review.
blockers.fix: File the request before you submit for review.

blockers.symptom: Submissions blocked for a period after repeated rejections
blockers.cause: Review cooldown, which gets longer each time it repeats.
blockers.fix: Fix every issue the reviewer raised and pass the automated checks before resubmitting.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so you need your own Dev Dashboard app from the start. Copy its client ID and secret into an OAuth2 auth config, and add Composio's callback URL as an allowed redirection URL. Confirm the exact callback path in your Composio project: both /api/v1/auth-apps/add and /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback have appeared. The authorize URL is https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize, so each connection needs the store subdomain. Trim the long default scope list to what you actually use.

open_questions: Which Composio callback should go in Allowed redirection URLs: backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add or /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback? Check your Composio auth config.
There is no official review turnaround. Reports range from 5-10 business days (unverified claim of an official figure) to 7-14 business days (third party).

Are expiring offline access tokens required for new public apps from April 2026? The only source is a vendor blog. A third-party post also says Dev Dashboard client-credentials tokens expire after 24 hours. Confirm how Composio handles refresh.
The full App Store requirements checklist (app-store-requirements and pass-app-review pages) wasn't retrieved, so there may be more requirements.
Partner account prerequisites beyond the one-time fee (Partner Program agreement, org role, business verification) and the exact fee amount weren't confirmed.
Where exactly credentials and protected-data requests live (Dev Dashboard vs Partner Dashboard) was only partly confirmed.
Can a Composio-backed agent with no merchant-facing UI pass the review rules (OAuth starting from the admin install, redirect to app UI)? You may need to build a small embedded or landing app.
